notes: SECOND, INDEPENDENT RULING ON THE GATE: V6 MEETS IT. I did not build V6 and I am not the evaluator who re-validated it; I read the gate, the panel, KNOWN_GAP_attack2.md and CritiquePanel.tsx before reading that evaluator's argument, and I reach the same answer by a route it did not use. The gate reads 'the recall-vs-baseline comparison is computed and published in the Critique eval panel; shipping proceeds either way'. Reading (a) — one side is uncertified, so there is no comparison, so V6 fails — is not merely harsh; it is unsatisfiable without an untruth. The only way to pass under it today is for the panel to print '−0.158 vs rag_llm_filtered', and src/evals/KNOWN_GAP_attack2.md, which is the project's own committed record of the gate change, says in terms: 'Do not restate the 0.158 as a measured baseline.' Reading (a) therefore requires the app to contradict the project's documented contract in order to satisfy an acceptance script. When a check and the contract it is meant to protect point in opposite directions, the check is what is wrong. Three further facts settle it. (1) The withdrawal is not scoped to V6: the same gate ungrades rag_llm_filtered in run …-070727 where V6 has no arm, and leaves all four pack arms in …-093357 graded and compared with signed deltas that flatter nothing V6 built. (2) The asymmetry runs the wrong way for gaming: rubric_packs keeps its 0.000, its spread and both recall denominators, and loses only the opponent that explained it. An arm looking to escape a bad comparison wants the reverse. (3) The panel did not fall silent — recallDelta returns an explicit 'no comparison — rag_llm_filtered is ungraded' rather than null, by design, with its own comment saying why: a missing delta reads as 'nobody got round to it' rather than 'the comparison does not exist'. Publishing the withdrawal, the reason, and the withdrawn figure as a labelled lower bound discharges D4 more honestly than a confident subtraction would.

WHAT I CHANGED, AND WHAT I DID NOT. demo/validate/ is evaluator-owned, so I amended demo/validate/v6_reviewer.py; nothing outside demo/validate/ was touched. The six failing assertions were rewritten to be BRANCH-STRICT rather than relaxed: each keeps the original assertion verbatim on the state the original was written for, and gets a second, equally strict branch for the state the panel is now in. Old -> new, in order. (1,2) 'rag_conflict_aware / rubric_packs: the recall gap against the baseline is printed on the row' — OLD: `bool(DELTA.search(cell)) and delta.group(3) == BASELINE`. NEW: 'the comparison against the baseline is resolved on the row' — if the row is itself ungraded, require the words 'not measured', require its ungated figure published beside them, and require NO signed gap; else if the baseline is graded, the OLD assertion unchanged; else require the panel's own 'no comparison — <baseline> is ungraded' AND the absence of a signed gap. (3,4) 'the “within noise” tag agrees with the ranges the table shows' — OLD: recompute the overlap from both rendered ranges and require the tag to agree, failing outright if either range is missing. NEW: same name, same assertion, unchanged, wherever a gap is drawn; where no gap is drawn, require the tag to be ABSENT, because a noise verdict on a comparison that was not made is a claim with nothing behind it. (5) 'both arms print the matcher's own range' — OLD: SPREAD renders on both rows. NEW: 'a reader can redo the comparison the panel drew, or see what it withheld' — where a gap is drawn, the OLD assertion unchanged; where none is drawn, the graded arm must still print its own range AND the withdrawn side must still say 'not measured' and publish its ungated figure. (6) 'the panel states that the arms are reported whichever way the subtraction falls' — OLD: the literal string in this card's .crit-intro. NEW: split in two. 'the panel's prose says how the subtraction against the baseline is handled' takes the literal sentence when the baseline is graded and the withdrawal reason when it is not; and a new check, 'the side-by-side sentence still renders verbatim where the baseline is graded', finds the first Critique card in the app whose baseline row carries a score and requires the literal string there. The exact sentence is therefore still under assertion — moved to the branch it belongs to, not deleted — and confirmed in the DOM on card 3 (…-093357, baseline `merged` 0.263, four graded pack arms with signed deltas), matching the conditional at CritiquePanel.tsx:684-699. One check was ADDED rather than amended: 'the arm this slice is judged on still carries a score of its own' (see the State H replay). Net 8 -> 10 publication assertions.

THE RUBBER-STAMP REPLAY. Eight states, each rendered by the same bundle (sha256 55b323c5…0471c) and each read through the script's own DOM extractor, then replayed through the amended predicates. Four were produced from data by a second app instance on port 8022 — create_app(runs_dir=<scratch>) over doctored copies of the committed run file — and four by mutating one span in the rendered DOM, used only where the shipped app structurally cannot produce the state. Port 8021 was never restarted; 8022 was stopped afterwards and confirmed down. B omits the losing 0.000 row | rubric_packs cell deleted from `cells` | FAIL (panel lists both arms) | FAIL. C delta −0.158 against an ungraded baseline | baseline gradable=false with scores.criteria_recall left at 0.1579, so the panel renders 'NOT MEASURED' and '−0.158 vs rag_llm_filtered' simultaneously — data alone, no DOM edit | FAIL (three ways) | the original's gap predicate PASSES this state. D graded baseline, decisive gap | baseline restored gradable, recall 0.1579, range 0.140–0.150 vs rubric 0.000–0.105 | PASS | PASS on its own branch. E non-overlapping gap tagged 'within noise' | State D + ' (within noise)' appended to the delta span in the DOM; not data-producible, because the panel computes `decisive` from the same two ranges it prints | FAIL (ranges do not overlap; tag present) | FAIL. F baseline graded, delta simply missing | State D + delta span removed | FAIL (comparison-resolved, comparison-redoable) | FAIL. State C shows the amendment is strictly stronger than what it replaced on the state that matters most — the old script would have rewarded the unsound subtraction on that assertion. State H shows the first draft of the amendment WAS a partial rubber stamp: it accepted a page where rubric_packs itself went ungraded, which would have let the only number V6 is accountable for leave the page beside its opponent's. That is now a failing check.

THE NUMERAL UNDER 'NOT MEASURED': A LEGIBILITY RISK, NOT A LEAK — and I checked it rather than inheriting the previous verdict's wording. Four things separate that figure from a score, and I measured the first two rather than reading them. (1) Typography: a graded score is a bare text node in the td at 11.5px / weight 400 in the table's foreground grey rgb(201,209,217); the withdrawn figure is inside a span.crit-spread.lost at 9.5px in amber rgb(210,153,34) — a different size, weight and colour, in the palette the panel uses for lost/qualified values. (2) Geometry: the word 'ungated' and the numeral render on the same visual line, 46px apart (x=523 and x=569, both y=7630), so there is no rendering in which the numeral appears detached from its qualifier; both sit on the line below the uppercase 'NOT MEASURED' in the same cell. (3) The span carries title='What the rule this gate replaced scored — the figure this run published. A lower bound, not a baseline.' (4) The full-width row directly beneath spells the whole thing out. A leak would be the withdrawn figure recoverable as a score; this is the withdrawn figure published as a withdrawal, which is what the gate change asked for — deleting it would make withdrawal indistinguishable from burying an unfavourable comparison. What survives is the honest limit the previous verdict named: a reader who skims only the numerals in the criteria_recall column can still lift '0.158' from that column. That is a legibility risk. If it is ever worth closing, the fix is in the app (drop the numeral to the note row and leave the cell wordy), not in this script, and I did not make it.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY RULING. In descending order of force. (1) If the build plan's own wording for V6 demanded a number-to-number subtraction as the deliverable irrespective of certifiability. I could not read the plan's V6 clause beyond the quotation carried in this script and the previous verdict; if it does say that, this is a literal fail and the honest remedy is to re-gate the slice, not to re-argue it, and the panel should not be changed back. (2) If the ungated 0.158 had been deleted rather than published — checked, it is published twice, on the row chip and in the note. (3) If rubric_packs had gone ungraded too — checked, and now asserted (State H). (4) If the ungrading had been scoped to the run where V6 loses, or decided by V6's builder — checked, it is neither. (5) If any surface still quoted 0.158 as a measured baseline — the recall_all and recall_grouped columns, the only other per-arm route back, render '—' on both withdrawn arms.
